t_r_convention: t,r : [B,1] with r <= t; t=0 is data, t=1 is noise; u_fn(z,t_,r_) = net.u(z, ppg, t_, t_-r_)
z_t: z_t = (1 - t) * x + t * e   with tt = t.reshape(-1,1,1)
v_tangent: u_theta(z_t, ppg, t, 0) under torch.no_grad() when not supplied (boundary condition, gradient-free)
reduction_order: square -> flatten(1).sum(1) over (channel,time) -> multiply per-sample w -> mean over batch
temporal_reduction: SUM over time, NOT mean — a mean-1 structure weight therefore preserves the delta2 scale
ecg_preprocessing: 128 Hz, 8 s = 1024 samples, ECG 0.5 Hz high-pass Butterworth order 4 filtfilt, per-window z-score then min-max to [-1,1]

underspecification_resolved.question: is the adaptive weight w computed from the unweighted or the structure-weighted delta2?
underspecification_resolved.decision: UNWEIGHTED — so w is bit-identical between arms U and S for identical inputs
underspecification_resolved.why: spec §7 requires preserving the existing weighting exactly and permits exactly one algorithmic difference; deriving w from the structure-weighted delta2 would be a second difference

structure_weight_shape: [B,1,T], broadcasts over the channel axis only, carries no gradient
arm_U_equivalence: structure_weight == 1 must reproduce the baseline loss bit-exactly (unit-tested)
